scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The missing tray
scenes.caption: Reva brings a labelled tray to the imaginary school seed exchange. Nikhil cannot find its matching packet on a crowded shelf. Their teacher supplies fictional records and asks whose difficulty a proposed AI helper should address.
scenes.speech: Reva brings a labelled tray to the imaginary school seed exchange. Nikhil cannot find its matching packet on a crowded shelf. Their teacher supplies fictional records and asks whose difficulty a proposed A I helper should address.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Two different needs
scenes.caption: The shelf volunteer wants faster searches. The seed club wants fewer wrong matches. Reva records both needs: saving time while returning the wrong packet would fail the people using the exchange, even if the technology looked impressive.
scenes.speech: The shelf volunteer wants faster searches. The seed club wants fewer wrong matches. Reva records both needs: saving time while returning the wrong packet would fail the people using the exchange, even if the technology looked impressive.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Measure the starting point
scenes.caption: For 10 invented searches, the printed index takes 30 minutes altogether and gives 2 wrong matches. Nikhil records this baseline. They will compare another method using equivalent searches and the same measurements, rather than impressions about volunteers.
scenes.speech: For 10 invented searches, the printed index takes 30 minutes altogether and gives 2 wrong matches. Nikhil records this baseline. They will compare another method using equivalent searches and the same measurements, rather than impressions about volunteers.
scenes.dialogue: A baseline is a recorded comparison.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: A testable promise
scenes.caption: Reva proposes at most 20 minutes and at most 2 wrong matches on 10 separate searches. Choose whether this measurable goal fits their investigation better than promising a smart shelf or judging which pupils deserve seed packets.
scenes.speech: Reva proposes at most 20 minutes and at most 2 wrong matches on 10 separate searches. Choose whether this measurable goal fits their investigation better than promising a smart shelf or judging which pupils deserve seed packets.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Keep the card small
scenes.caption: The comparison records duration, match correctness and the method used. Names, addresses and family incomes are unnecessary for this fictional trial. A teacher checks the proposed fields, while volunteers remain responsible for checking which packet a requester receives.
scenes.speech: The comparison records duration, match correctness and the method used. Names, addresses and family incomes are unnecessary for this fictional trial. A teacher checks the proposed fields, while volunteers remain responsible for checking which packet a requester receives.
scenes.dialogue: Measure the task, not private lives.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Return to the need
scenes.caption: Define the question, prepare permitted examples, build a candidate, test against the index and review results. In the lab, complete the problem card and cycle. Keeping the printed index is a valid outcome if the evidence favours it.

scenes.dialogue: The useful result may be simple.
